subject: Re: NBA X Encord POC data sharing
text:
Hi James,
Great talking today. As discussed, our near-term goal is to stand up an event-centric, multi-angle annotation workflow for jump-shot arm-contact and ship a pilot “smart queue” that surfaces ~20 high-value plays per game with higher precision than our current distance-rule baseline.
I’ve attached two short docs for your review:

  *
Annotation design & workflow (Encord-ready) — ontology, angle attributes, temporal segments, synchronized mosaic labeling, ambiguity reasons, adjudication, exporter contracts, quality gates, active-learning hooks, and versioning.
  *
Multi-Angle Data Strategy, Annotation & Modeling — end-to-end plan (data collection/EDA, multi-view fusion, VLM captions) and the precision/recall target for the pilot.

What we’re asking from Encord (examples + guidance)
1) Platform fit — please confirm Encord can implement/configure:

  *
Event-centric ontology: one parent event_id with all camera views as children; single source-of-truth label per event propagated to all angles; angle-aware attributes (camera_view, view_quality, contact_visibility).
  *
Precise temporal segments with pre_contact_ms / post_contact_ms; minimal contact taxonomy(shooting_arm_contact + optional contact_point, timing); Shooter/Defender tracks linked via potential_contact(); side-by-side synchronized mosaic for labeling; ambiguity class with reason codes; dual-annotator + adjudication; exporter contracts (events.jsonl, views.jsonl, tracks.jsonl); submission quality gates.
  *
Active-learning hooks (uncertainty, angle-prediction disagreement, pose-vs-pixel conflicts), angle-utility scoring, and versioning of ontology/guidelines.

2) Concrete examples to share back:

  *
An Encord ontology JSON + task template implementing the above (roles: Shooter, Defender; attributes + validators; helpful keyboard shortcuts).
  *
A brief demo or job showing the synchronized mosaic UI and your recommended attribute dropdowns.
  *
Sample exports matching the contracts (events.jsonl / vie

subject: Re: Encord <> PlayOn | Unlocking FY27 revenue by scaling in-house annotations
text:
James,

Thanks for your patience in our response to this matter.  I’ve included a brief description of project that we’re considering undertaking and would be interested in understanding how you might assist us.

Regarding data sharing, the main input here would be a basketball video.  If you’d like us to share some of our videos, I can forward an NDA form to you — just let me know.
And, if you have any further questions, please let me know.

Regards,
Ed Goetze

Basketball Shot Detection
For a given basketball game video, create a structured output (e.g., JSON) that describes the attempted shots in the video that includes at least the following information: time/frame of shot, shot outcome, team & player identification (e.g., jersey number and color), shot type (free, two, three).

Some of the high level aspects of the system are as follows.

Core Processing Pipeline

  *   Automated Video Analysis: System automatically processes new game videos when uploaded to cloud storage
  *   Video Ingestion Service: Service that triggers automatically on video uploads
Event Detection & Analysis

  *   Shot Event Detection: System identifies timestamps/frames where a basketball and hoop are in close proximity
  *   Clip Generation: Creates video clips around potential shot events
  *   AI-Powered Analysis: Analyze clips to extract structured data
Data Output & Storage

  *   Structured Shot Data: System provides detailed information including:
     *   Shot outcome (made/missed)
     *   Shooting team/player identification
     *   Shot type classification (1, 2, or 3-point shots)
  *   JSON Results Storage: Structured output stored in cloud/database storage
  *
Persistent Event Log: Searchable/query-able log of all analyzed shot events for each game
Quality Assurance & Documentation

  *   End-to-End Testing: Complete pipeline testing from video upload to final result generation
  *   System Documentation: Comprehensive documentation covering architecture, service configurati

subject: Re: Encord CA
text:
Hi James,

Thank you so much for your thoughtful note. While I am of course disappointed to hear the outcome, I truly appreciate the time you and the team have taken with me throughout this process.

I want to share that I do fully understand the requirements of the role and I view this position as the natural and exciting next step in my career. It’s exactly the type of role where I can contribute meaningfully from day one, while continuing to grow and develop internally over time.

When I first applied for the role in San Francisco, the feedback was never around being overqualified, which is why I am surprised to hear that concern now. That said, I value transparency and would welcome any specific feedback you might be able to share, as it will help me continue to improve.

What has kept me motivated through two interview cycles is my genuine belief that Encord is where I belong. Culture fit is very important to me, and I see this as a long-term opportunity to contribute, not as a short-term step. The growth path you described in your email mirrors exactly the journey I envisioned for myself at Encord.

If there’s any room to reconsider, I’d be grateful. I truly believe my skills, motivation, and commitment to the company’s success could add value right away, while also allowing me to build toward the closing experience you’re looking for. 

Thank you again for your time, candor, and consideration. I’ve very much enjoyed getting to know the team and learning more about Encord.

Best regards,
Merve
